assign.now: wrote the five sentences before touching anything, took before shots

log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES (before). what: a bare word list turned wall of 12 study cards (Journey, Padding, Scale, Layout, Navigation, Color, Type, Controls, Vocabulary, System, Themes, Spacing), each a generic material icon plus a two-line description, no picture. use: click any card to open that study in the column beside it. goal: pick one of 12 design questions to read about the site's own screenshots. hard: 2/5 - the intent is clear (a menu of studies) but every card looks the same (icon+text), so nothing signals which study is richest, newest, or most worth opening first. better: swap the generic icon for a real screenshot from each study's own shots/ folder - the studies already collected them, the index just wasn't using them.

before measurements at http://localhost:8110/imagine/design/, .page-column-body.page-column-full is the real box (.page.active-page is display:contents, zero rect - a Miller-columns peer, not a box; walked the ancestor chain to find it). 1280: width used 99.9% (1279/1280), column height 860px, no internal scroll (scrollHeight==clientHeight). 3440: width used 99.97% (3439/3440), column height 852px, no internal scroll. Both already ~100% width used because this page already carries width:"full" (fixed 2026-09-04, per its own readme) - the site-wide known ~1856px columns dead-band does not apply to a full-width column, so width/dead-space were not this task's problem to solve.

assign.now: built and measured the 3-column-card alternative for real

log.msg: ALTERNATIVE LAYOUT tried: the owner's 3-column card (title+intro left, a real screenshot centre, a one-line finding right), one row per study, stacked - built for real in page.js/design.css, not just considered. Shape borrowed from /imagine/layouts/layouts.css .layouts-card and /imagine/research/research-front.css .rfront-card (same flex-wrap + rem-floor + calc((floor - 100%) * 999) stack-term trick), reused rather than reinvented, added a design- prefix to css-scopes.txt for the new .design-card family.

First build measured 5888px tall at 1280 and a startling 19609px at 3440 - a real bug, not the honest cost of the shape: .design-stage (the screenshot column) had a floor (max(46%, stack)) but no ceiling, so at 3440 a flat 1280x800 screenshot got scaled past 1500px tall per card. Every track needs a floor AND a ceiling (the layout skill's own rule) - fixed with a max-width on the stage and on the card itself, capped at 76em and centred rather than stretched to the full full-width column ("accept the gutter" per the skill, since a screenshot has a real native resolution and stretching it past that is pixels for nothing).

After the fix: 1280 -> 4324px tall (was 860px), 3440 -> 5280px tall (was 852px). Both still pass the three invariants and both use ~100% of the width (unsurprising - width was never in question here, height is). REVERTED: for a front door whose whole job is showing a stranger twelve choices at a glance, a 5-6x taller page is a real cost the tile wall does not pay - a reader sees all twelve options in one screen today; with the card row they would scroll past two or three before reaching the rest. This is the same shape /imagine/research/ correctly kept for its four topic cards - four rows of scroll is a fair trade there; twelve is a different number. Numbers and reasoning written up at public/imagine/design/doc/layout-alternative.md so the receipts outlive this log.

assign.now: made the tile wall more visual with real screenshots

log.msg: MORE VISUAL, kept: the tile wall stayed, but 10 of 12 cards now show a real screenshot from that study's own shots/ folder instead of a generic material-icon tile - Journey, Padding, Scale, Layout, Navigation, Color, Type, Controls, Themes, Spacing. Implementation: one shared .design-shot CSS rule (design.css, same trick as journey/journey.css's own .journey-shot - object-fit:cover fills Page.css's page-preview-thumb box) plus one preview(nav) override per child page.js, each pointing at one real file already in that study's shots/. Page.class.js's own preview_card() drops the two-line description once a thumb is present (by design, framework-wide) - the picture replaces the paragraph, which is exactly the owner's ask. vocabulary/ and system/ are pure prose/data (no picture of a page to show), so they were left as icon+description rather than faking a screenshot.

themes/ had no shots/ of its own (its subject IS a live page) - took one screenshot of the live /imagine/design/themes/ page for its card, saved to themes/shots/mock-wall.jpg. scale/'s first pick (gallery.jpg) turned out to be a near-blank 3440 screenshot that read as a broken thumbnail once cropped small - caught on the after-1280 screenshot review, swapped for mag.jpg (a bold magazine headline, legible at thumbnail size) from the same shots/ folder. Verified all 10 image srcs return 200 and decode (naturalWidth > 0) via a Playwright response listener.

Net effect on height (a bonus, not the goal): dropping the description text made the thumbed cards shorter than the old icon+2-line-description cards, even with a picture added - page height went 860px -> 786px at 1280, and 852px -> 734px at 3440. Width used unchanged (~100% both times, already full-width). Invariants re-checked after the change: no card left edge at x:0 (leftmost card starts 20px/1280, 49px/3440, the column's own padding), no prose past the measure (only vocabulary/system keep body text, ~272-318px wide, far under ~40em), no framed box touches the container edge. All three pass at 1280 and 3440.

PERSISTENCE: none. grep -rn store()|localStorage across public/imagine/design/ found exactly one hit, in themes/page.js - a written proposal's prose explaining how page.store() COULD work, quoted inside a note() call, never an actual invocation. No real .store( call anywhere in the realm. The design realm remembers nothing about a visitor; baseline() does not apply.

UI-TEST: drove a real click on the Padding card's stretched link (.page--design .page-previews > .page-preview:nth-child(2) .page-preview-link) at 1280. Result: url went /imagine/design/ -> /imagine/design/padding/, the Design column stayed open and shrank rather than the page reloading, the Padding column opened beside it with its real content (breadcrumb Imagine > Design > Padding, heading The ladder) - the owner's 'a clearly defined area swaps content' shape, already true of this columns host before tonight. Zero console errors during the gesture (steps.json's errors field empty on every step).

CONSOLE: swept all 12 children plus the index at both 1280 and 3440 with a fresh headless page per url (page.on(console/pageerror)) - zero errors everywhere, before and after the edit. Also confirmed no doc/*.md link inside any page.js in this realm (the router-miss trap named in the brief) - none exist; the one .md-suffixed link this task itself introduced (readme.md's own pointer to doc/layout-alternative.md) was rewritten to the routed form /imagine/design/doc/layout-alternative/ before landing, curl-verified 200.

log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES (after). what: a wall of 12 study cards, 10 of them showing a real screenshot from that study instead of a generic icon. use: click any card - the picture and the title are the whole pitch now, no description text competing with it. goal: same as before, pick one of 12 design questions and open it; now the picture itself hints which study is which before you read a word. hard: 1/5 - a picture of the actual thing (a padding ladder, a dark-mode page, a resize handle) reads faster than an icon+description ever could, and the two text-only cards (vocabulary, system) are now the visible exception rather than the rule, which is honest since they are the two studies with no picture to show. better: the two text-only cards could still get a small generated glyph of their own data (a tag cloud swatch for vocabulary, a rule-count badge for system) instead of the shared default icon, closing the gap between all 12 without inventing a fake screenshot.

REFINEMENT to the width/dead-space numbers: the brief's own boxes.right recipe measures the widest ELEMENT in the column, which for a full-width column is the container itself (~100% trivially) regardless of whether the cards inside actually reach it - not a meaningful content measure here. Measured the cards directly instead: at 3440 the 12-card grid (--column 20em) packs 9 per row (350px each, symmetric ~49px gutter, row1 reaches x:3390 of 3440 = 98.5%) and wraps the remaining 3 to a second row that only reaches x:1147 - a real 2293px trailing dead band. This is identical before and after (same 12 items, same --column, untouched by the visual/layout work) - it is the tile wall's own known trade-off (a 12-item auto-fill grid has a remainder row at some widths), not a defect this task introduced, and not one of the three invariants (no box touches x:0, no prose past measure, no framed box off the padded edge - all three still pass with this row2 present). Reported honestly rather than restating the trivial ~100%.
